verdictSummary: Both slices verify as designed and claimed. a1's fix is a genuine, minimal, correctly-scoped canonicalization workaround (matches the admission brief's own explicit recommendation to sanitize the call site rather than the shared canonicalizer). a2's create-path seeding is a real structural-capability extension with no new event type, no mode flip, no schema change, and correctly gated by both the existing mode-off return and a landed-every-event guard. Red-first is genuine and reproduced exactly as claimed. All cited file:line references check out exactly. All gates are green. Merge-tree against the pinned main SHA (17525370e) is clean. One coverage gap found by independent mutation (the partial-persist guard in ServerMatchHostEvents.ts is untested) is NOT a hidden defect -- the preparer's own receipt already discloses it verbatim as S7a-Q4 and characterizes it correctly as a non-blocking scope note. No blocking defects. Recommend two stacked PRs as detailed in packagingRecommendation.

findings.text: withoutUndefinedProperties is defined in MatchStreamJournalMirror.ts:94-109 and applied exactly once, inside toMatchJournalBatch, to matchEvent before it is used to build the per-event IMatchJournalEnvelope (MatchStreamJournalMirror.ts:173). Both canonicalization passes downstream -- the command-identity digest (EventJournalCommandIdentity.ts -> canonicalizeJsonV1 over the whole batch) and each event's own digest (SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:235 canonicalizeEventDigestV1) -- consume this one already-stripped envelope, so the two passes cannot disagree about which form of the event they are hashing.

The stripped form is a fixed point of DurableMatchStore's own durable form. DurableMatchStore.ts:843 writes JSON.stringify(event) for a batch append, and (at the pre-a2 line numbers, i.e. the state right after 5f7b10799) DurableMatchStore.ts:1163 and :1269 read it back with JSON.parse -- an own-enumerable undefined-valued property does not survive that stringify/parse round trip, so withoutUndefinedProperties(event) and JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(event)) agree on every event this codebase actually persists (they diverge only on values withoutUndefinedProperties does NOT drop -- functions, symbols, Dates, BigInts -- which is deliberate, see F3). After a2 lands the file grows by 56 lines and the same statements sit at :843 (unchanged) and :1219/:1325 (getEvents' JSON.parse) -- verified both states directly, no drift in meaning.

The shared canonicalizer (EventJournalCanonicalizer.ts) is untouched by this stack (not in the four commits' touched-file list). Its canonicalize() switch (lines 60-73) has a default: arm that calls fail('unsupported-value', ...) for any typeof outside {boolean, number, string, object} -- typeof undefined === 'undefined' falls into that default and throws EventJournalCanonicalizationError('unsupported-value'), which is exactly the throw the a1 red suite measures and the a1 fix suite still exercises for a genuinely non-representable value (a function, typeof 'function', also hits the same default arm). The canonicalizeJsonV1 entry point (line 123-125) is a thin wrapper over the same canonicalize().

SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:430 writes payloadJson: canonicalizeJsonV1(event.payload) at commit time, and SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:345 re-canonicalizes the parsed form on read and compares against the stored event_digest (canonicalizeEventDigestV1(event).digest !== event.eventDigest -> integrity(...)). Both line numbers match the review brief's citations exactly.

seedJournalFromInitialEvents (DurableMatchStore.ts, new method) mirrors the GameCreated + GameStarted events the caller hands it -- no new event type is introduced anywhere in the diff. Its expectedRevision is nextMatchSequenceAfter(null), which resolves to the exported constant MATCH_FIRST_SEQUENCE = 0 (matchStoreBranchSegmentReader.ts:50,67-73) -- i.e. the empty-journal revision, matching an empty log's expectation on both arms of the consult. It is called through mirrorCommittedBatch (the SAME method appendCommandBatch uses), which still opens with `if (getCombatJournalAuthorityMode() === 'off') return;` (DurableMatchStore.ts:1000) -- the pre-existing early return, unmodified by this stack, gates the seed path exactly as it gates every command batch.

seedJournalFromInitialEvents is declared as an OPTIONAL method on IMatchStore (IMatchStore.ts, `seedJournalFromInitialEvents?(...)`) -- a genuine structural-flag capability, matching appendCommandBatch's own optionality. InMemoryMatchStore.ts implements appendCommandBatch but does NOT implement seedJournalFromInitialEvents (grepped, zero hits) -- confirming the in-memory store lacks the capability and its behavior is unchanged by this stack. persistInitialEvents (ServerMatchHostEvents.ts) calls it only when `persisted === ctx.events.length && ctx.store.seedJournalFromInitialEvents` -- i.e. only after every opening event landed AND only when the store offers the capability.

A create at mode 'off' writes nothing to the journal -- reproduced live: the a2 suite's third row ('seeds nothing at all while the cutover mode is off') passes at HEAD and journalEventIds() is empty in that row. No migration, no schema change, no new dependency: git diff --name-only 423381ff0..b9ab4a668 touches only the four production files plus the two new test files, all under src/lib/multiplayer/server/.

openQuestionAssessment.text: Seed idempotency rests on the journal's command-identity check (duplicateIsSuccess treats any duplicate-command as success), which would also swallow a genuinely divergent retry (two different opening logs for one match id) rather than surfacing it as a conflict. No production path produces that today.
openQuestionAssessment.assessment: NOT a blocking defect for the admitted scope. COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_MODE is a hardcoded 'off' const with no env read (matchJournalAuthority.ts:18-19, verified directly) -- every path this slice adds is unreachable in production. The divergent-retry scenario requires a live command-batch stream at a non-off mode, which does not exist today. Concur with the preparer's own severity ('medium, owner ruling wanted before any flip') and recommend it be carried forward explicitly to S7-d, where the migration-state machine is meant to replace command-identity-based idempotency with a durable per-match 'seeded' fact -- exactly as S7a-Q2 itself proposes.

openQuestionAssessment.text: Seeding at create makes S5-R1's inherited warning MORE reachable: a rewound match now has a head, so at mode 'shadow' its later live-path batches would meet the rewound-stream refusal and pin the shadow-mismatch counter above zero. No row here covers a seeded-then-rewound match at 'shadow'.
openQuestionAssessment.assessment: NOT a blocking defect for the admitted scope, for the same reason as S7a-Q2 -- mode 'shadow' is reachable only through _setCombatJournalAuthorityModeForTests, never in production while COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_MODE stays the hardcoded 'off' const. This is a genuine residual: it should be carried forward and closed before any process is EVER run at 'shadow' against real traffic (S7-d's stated job, per the S6 receipt's own S6-R1/S4-R1 framing). Concur with the preparer's characterization ('medium, inherited and NOT closed') -- recommend it be tracked explicitly as a precondition-check item in whatever S7-d's task list or design.md ends up naming as the shadow-mode readiness gate, rather than silently assumed closed by this slice.
